breakdown.description: For curved flow, pressure is higher on the outside of the turn to provide the required centripetal force; stating pressure increases toward the center reverses the correct direction of the pressure gradient.
breakdown.reason: The agent failed to correct the user's physical misconception. The original prompt incorrectly stated that pressure increases toward the center of curvature. The agent's final output concludes, "The pressure on the inner side of the streamline is 2000 Pa higher than the pressure on the outer side," which is the same physical error. The ground truth corrects this by defining the normal direction `n` as pointing outward, implying pressure is higher on the outer side of the curve.
